sartor-resartus-the-life-and-opinions-of:
Thomas Carlyle published Sartor Resartus in 1831, giving the book a subtitle that presents it as the life and opinions of Herr Teufelsdrockh. The opening chapter, called Preliminary, starts with a complaint. Learning has grown for five thousand years and more, Carlyle argues, yet almost no deep study in philosophy or history takes clothes as its subject.

He sharpens the point by naming fields that now look settled or complete. Astronomy can predict the planets, and earth science can explain how worlds form. Thinkers have produced accounts of rent, value, language, and much more. Clothes alone, he says, have been passed over, even though dress covers the body and shapes how a person meets the world. The rest of the book takes up that neglected subject.
